newsitem.title: USA: G7 in Denver to address market reforms-Summers.
newsitem.headline: G7 in Denver to address market reforms-Summers.

text.p: Group of Seven financial leaders meeting next weekend in Denver will focus on market reforms and cooperative regulation to minimize systemic risks, said U.S. Treasury Deputy Secretary Lawrence Summers.
Citing the recent currency crises in Thailand and the Czech Republic, plus the Mexican peso collapse in late 1994, Summers said current G7 proposals would help reduce the risk of future debacles.

"We managed the Mexico crisis successfully, but we did so in an ad hoc fashion. With the new proposals, we believe that the international community will be better able to help forestall a future sovereign financial crisis and to manage the impact if one does occur," said Summers at a luncheon.

Tighter International Monetary Fund surveillance of nations borrowing in international capital markets and formal emergency credit facilities should minimize the damage from future sovereign financial crises, Summers said.
"It is hard to overemphasize how important a factor transparency is in bringing problems to the light of day before they become serious," Summers said.
Summers said many emerging market nations had made good progress in moving toward internationally-accepted standards for market regulation.
"Observers have been surprised at the extent of progress that has been achieved over the last year," he added.

The G7 in Denver will endorse initiatives to develop a global system of regulations to supervise internationally active firms as well as to reduce foreign exchange settlement risk and improve disclosure of derivatives exposures, said Summers.
But Summers added that regulators should endeavor to preserve the current flexibility of financial markets, which helps reduce volatility and risk in many ways.
"Keeping the supervisory system abreast of innovation without constraining innovation will continue to be an important priority," he added.
